member.title: Member Pledge
member.why: Why we ask: every member signs it. It’s the promise that keeps the Society’s rooms, events and channels kind and safe for everyone.
member.body: As a member of the Society of Arts and Letters, I will treat everyone with courtesy and every piece of work with care. I will critique the work and never the person. I will respect consent, before a camera and on the page. I will be honest with the Society’s money and its members’ trust. I will keep what is confidential, keep my word or say early that I cannot, and leave every room better than I found it.

agreement.title: Publication Agreement
agreement.body:
By signing, you agree to the Society’s terms for publishing your work, from the Policy Manual:

9.1 Creators own their work. By presenting or submitting it, they give the Society permission to show, perform, publish and archive it for the purpose agreed, and nothing more.

9.2 Everyone who works on a Society project is credited by name in its program, masthead or end credits, unless they ask not to be.

9.5 Plagiarism in any Society program leads to withdrawal of the work and may lead to action under P1.

10.1 Creative work submitted to Qirtas, the Mutanabbi Prize, the Company and the Society’s events must be the member’s own. Work drafted, written, translated or generated by AI is not eligible. Spellcheck and basic grammar tools are fine.

The purpose agreed is publication in Qirtas, online and in print, and the Society’s archive.

twoStep.title: Two-step sign-in
twoStep.body: If they lost their phone and have no recovery code left, reset it. Their authenticator app and recovery codes are removed, they set up new ones at their next sign-in, and they get an email saying so.
twoStep.description: Remove {name}'s authenticator app and recovery codes? Do this only when they asked, after checking it’s really them.
twoStep.done: Reset. {name} sets up a new authenticator at their next sign-in.

departure.title: Left AUIB
departure.body: For a student Member who has left AUIB. A graduate becomes an Associate Member: same account and number, no vote and no office. Someone who left without graduating becomes a guest: same number and a Guest card, no vote, no role, and Hudhud takes them out of the members’ group after a week.
departure.graduatedDescription: {name} graduated: their class becomes Associate Member and any role they hold ends.
departure.leftDescription: {name} left AUIB without graduating: their account becomes a guest account with the same number, and any role they hold ends.

verification.title: Partner applications
verification.lede: Organizations that applied to partner with the Society, each with its memorandum signed by name. The Council votes on each at its meeting; the President then countersigns here under its adopted resolution, and the organization becomes a partner. Each partner then verifies its own people.
verification.decisionNote: Note to keep with the decision (optional)
verification.approveConfirm: Verify {email}? They become a member and can use the Diwan.
verification.rejectConfirm: Decline {email}? They will be told by email.
verification.signConfirm: Countersign the memorandum with {name} under the Council’s resolution? It becomes an active partner, and whoever applied leads its dashboard.
verification.declineConfirm: Decline {name}'s application? It stays on record.
verification.earlierLede: People who asked before partners verified their own. Approve only people you can place.
verification.noResolution: No adopted Council resolution to choose yet. The Council adopts it at its meeting, under that meeting’s minutes.
verification.signingAs: You countersign for the Society as

events.title: Events
events.lede: Every event on the term calendar: what’s coming, drafts and what’s past. Events are made in Notion’s Events database; open one here to see who booked, run its check-in and keep its parts.
events.campusNote: AUIB’s own dates come in every hour from the University’s public calendar.

event.notFound: No event with this link, or your roles don’t cover it.
event.questionsHint: Up to ten. Asked when someone books. A booking already carries their name on the platform, so there is no need to ask for it.
event.question: Question {number}

errors.questions: Each question needs its English and Arabic wording.

event.staffHint: Staff can check people in at this event only.
event.findHint: Type at least two letters of a name or the start of an email.

entryHint.rsvp: People book a place; the capacity and the waitlist apply.
entryHint.members: Members book a place; the capacity and the waitlist apply. It never appears publicly.

event.invitationsHint: Only the people invited (and the officers who run the event) see it.

links.title: Links
links.lede: Outside links for this event, such as the album played or the reading list. They show on the event’s page.
links.label: What it is

occasion.waiting: Waiting for Student Life’s written approval. The event is not published until it is recorded.
occasion.bySecretary: The General Secretary records the approval.
occasion.dateHint: The date on Student Life’s written approval. Clear it to withdraw the approval of an event not yet published.
occasion.approvedBy: Student Life approved this in writing on {date} ({by}).

parts.collectionLede: Link the campaign to its event, the fair: the event’s page then carries the collection, its catalog and its impact report.
parts.addLede: Every event has the same details. Add what this one needs; its page shows what it has.
parts.noMinutes: No minutes for this meeting yet. They are written in Notion (Work, Meetings) and come here when their Status is Minutes in the Diwan.

guests.title: Guests
guests.hint: Invite someone from outside AUIB by email. The link works for that address only, for fourteen days; they join as the Society’s guest, with a Guest card for the door.

checkIn.title: Check-in
checkIn.lede: Scan the ticket QR in a member’s Diwan, or their membership card. If the camera won’t work, look them up by name.
checkIn.cameraUnavailable: The camera isn’t available here. Use the lookup below.
checkIn.invalidTicket: That ticket isn’t valid for this event.
checkIn.unknownCode: That isn’t a SAL ticket or membership card.
checkIn.lookup: Look up by name or email
checkIn.cardNotLive: This card’s code isn’t live (a screenshot?). Ask to see the card on the member’s own phone.

content.title: Content
content.lede: Pages, notices, the homepage and the media library. Rich text is sanitized when saved and again when shown.
content.newsMoved: News is now written on Qirtas’s News desk.
content.pageSlugHint: Lowercase words and hyphens; use / for a section, for example about/traditions.
content.publishConfirm: Publish now? It appears on auibsal.org at once.
content.unpublishConfirm: Take this down from the site and keep it as a draft?
content.scheduleConfirm: Schedule this post? It is published on its own at the publish time.
content.newsletter: The Sunday Paper’s public list has {count} confirmed subscribers. They sign up at auibsal.org/sunday-paper; members who receive email get it too.

programmes.title: Events
programmes.lede: Every event is a standard event, with its shifts, needs, prompts and vote on its own page.

episodes.youtubeError: That isn’t a YouTube link or an 11-character video id.
episodes.careNote: Before publishing: releases signed, camera-shy members not shown, guests given their 48-hour review.

reels.urlError: Use an Instagram, TikTok or YouTube link (https://…).
reels.caption: Caption

rotas.deleteShiftConfirm: Delete this shift and its sign-ups?
rotas.stationHint: Volunteers you confirm on it, once trained, may attach photographed pages to live cards while it runs, and only then.

removals.lede: Requests to remove a photo or video (MEM-02): what the request points to on the site is hidden as it arrives; decide within two business days, take it down from the Society’s channels or decline with a reason.
removals.closeConfirm: Close this request? Write down what was done.

openings.lede: Openings on Get involved: team roles, event teams and Qalam mentors. Members who say they’re interested are listed here, and each one is also emailed to the event leads. Close the opening once it’s filled.
openings.title: Title
openings.replies: {count, plural, =0 {Nobody has replied yet} one {One member is interested} other {{count} members are interested}}
openings.closeConfirm: Close this opening? It leaves Get involved; the replies stay here.
openings.listLede: Every open role on Get involved: team roles, event teams and Qalam mentors. A role’s replies go through hiring: the Director of Membership runs it, and the role’s owner picks the person.

kindHints.role: A role the Society needs filled, chosen from its roles. New team members serve their first term on probation, then are confirmed.
kindHints.event_team: A place on one event’s team. Volunteer shifts are on the event’s own page.
kindHints.qalam_mentor: A mentor’s place in Qalam. Students never get accounts: record nothing about them here.

programmes.none: No event is yours to run yet. Roles are assigned on a member’s page.

pitches.title: Event proposals
pitches.lede: Ideas for new events that members sent. The President answers each one.

prompts.lede: The writing prompts for this event. Publish the ones its page should show as cards.

vote.lede: Choose up to three books and a closing time; members vote on the event’s page. You see the votes as they come; everyone else sees them once voting closes.
vote.noBooks: No books on this vote yet.
vote.author: Author
vote.closesOn: {count, plural, one {Closes {date} · {votes} vote so far} other {Closes {date} · {votes} votes so far}}
vote.removeBookConfirm: Remove this book from the vote?
vote.removeBallotConfirm: Remove this vote, its books and every vote cast?

sixWords.lede: Pages from the Typewriter Tour are typed on the Tour, never on the site. Type each page as written. Scan the writer’s membership card to make it theirs, or save it unsigned and attach it later. Every page is private until its writer chooses their profile or the Tour’s page.
sixWords.hint: The words, as typed on the page.
sixWords.scanToSave: Scan the writer’s card to save
sixWords.claimant: The member who claimed it (through Help Desk)

problems.notLive: That card’s code has expired. Ask them to open their card again and scan the live code.

import.title: The spring 2026 Tour
import.lede: Load the Tour’s scanned pages and the invitation list once. The files go from this browser to the site’s database and nowhere else. Loading them again updates what was loaded; nothing is sent until the President sends the invitations.
import.loaded: Loaded {pages} pages and {invitations} invitations; {attached} pages went straight to writers who already have an account.
import.status: Invitations: {waiting} waiting, {sent} sent, {joined} joined. Pages not yet claimed: {unclaimed}.
import.invitations: The invitations go list by list from Membership → Invitations.

sixWords.toTranscribe: Photographed at the station; its words not yet typed in.
sixWords.transcribeHint: Type the words exactly as on the page.

governance.title: Governance
governance.lede: Council terms, minutes and resolutions (draft until adopted), requests to Student Life and elections.

minutes.adoptConfirm: Mark these minutes adopted? Members will see them in the Diwan. Only do this after the vote.
minutes.draftNote: Drafts are visible only to minute-takers and governance managers.
minutes.locked: Adopted: this is the official copy and is locked.
minutes.fromNotion: Minutes are written in Notion (Work, Meetings) and come here when their Status is Minutes in the Diwan; the Council adopts them here. Meetings are events in Notion’s Events database.

resolutions.adoptedOnError: An adopted resolution needs its adoption date, and only then.
resolutions.missing: This resolution or its meeting is not here
resolutions.title: Resolutions of this meeting
resolutions.none: No resolutions recorded for this meeting.
resolutions.numberOnAdoption: The site numbers the resolution (RES-year-number) once it is adopted; failed motions are recorded only in the minutes.

elections.flagOff: Online elections are off (Settings → Feature flags).
elections.addPositions: Add the three Executive Board positions
elections.openVotingConfirm: Open voting now? Everyone on the voter list can vote online with their AUIB account until voting closes.
elections.countConfirm: Count now? Polls must have closed. Each seat needs a majority of the votes cast.
elections.ronWon: Reopen nominations won: the seat is filled by new nominations.
elections.dateError: Check the dates: nominations close after they open, voting opens after nominations close, and closes after it opens.

elections.noticeGiven: {count, plural, =0 {Notice given {date}. No one is on the voter list.} one {Notice given {date}. {n} person is on the voter list.} other {Notice given {date}. {n} people are on the voter list.}}
elections.startRunoffConfirm: Open the runoff now? It has the same voter list and these candidates, and closes in two days (within a week of this election).
elections.tiedDraw: Tied: draw lots at a public meeting, then record the result.
elections.recordLotConfirm: Record that {name} won the draw at a public meeting?
elections.votingPointAt: When the voting point is open

notion.title: Notion
notion.lede: The team’s workspace: projects, tasks, meetings and the handbook live there, and events and news are written and published from there. Every fifteen minutes the platform copies officers, event series, documents and Qirtas counts into it and publishes what is marked Ready to publish.
notion.notConfigured: Not connected. Add the SAL Platform connection’s token as NOTION_TOKEN on the auibsal project in Vercel, then redeploy.
notion.counts: {created} added, {updated} updated, {published} published, {refused} sent back for changes.
notion.noSyncYet: Connected; the first sync runs within five minutes.

notion.inviteHint: They hold a role in the Diwan but have no Notion account under their AUIB address. In Notion: Settings, People, Add members.
notion.inviteEmpty: Everyone holding a role is in the workspace.
notion.removeHint: In the workspace but holding no role in the Diwan. Remove them unless they own the workspace.

telegram.title: Telegram
telegram.lede: Hudhud, the Society’s Telegram bot: its username and connecting the Society’s group. The group’s welcome message, rules and moderation are set in Telegram itself.
telegram.usernameHint: Without the @, as set in BotFather; it ends in “bot”. Members see Connect Telegram in their profile once it is set.
telegram.connectHint: Add the bot to the group as an admin, then send this message in the group within 15 minutes.
telegram.notConfigured: Not set up yet: add {missing} to the auibsal project in Vercel, then redeploy.

email.lede: The Society’s own emails: bookings, Qirtas, the personal address link and the Sunday Paper.
email.notConfigured: Not sending: set {missing} (Supabase → Vault for the secrets).
email.stuck: {count} emails are waiting to be sent.

journal.title: Qirtas: Editions
journal.lede: Issues, pieces and contributors. Accepted work becomes a draft piece here; nothing from a submission is published before its author signs the Publication Agreement.

issue.notFound: No issue with this link, or your roles don’t cover it.
issue.publishConfirm: Publish this issue? It appears on auibsal.org at once; its published pieces go with it.
issue.printedHint: How many copies, who printed it and when. The Edition page shows it as one line once all three are filled in.
issue.launchNightHint: The event that launches this Edition. The Editions page shows it beside the call.

piece.titleHint: Fill the language(s) the piece is in.
piece.credit: Credit (for example, “Translated from the Arabic by …”)
piece.membersOnly: For members (listed publicly; only signed-in members read the text)
piece.notFound: No piece with this link, or your roles don’t cover it.
piece.agreementNeeded: The author hasn’t signed the Publication Agreement yet; publishing will wait for it.
piece.publishConfirm: Publish this piece? It appears on its issue’s page at once.

contributor.new: Add a member as a contributor
contributor.title: Contributors

byline.penNameHint: Only if the piece runs under a pen name. Readers see only the pen name.

pipeline.title: Qirtas: blind reading
pipeline.lede: The blind review of submissions, from intake to decision. Each person sees only their part: the Submissions Manager holds the key and never scores; readers and editors work from blind ids; author names appear only after a decision.
pipeline.noIssues: No issue has you in its review team yet.

reading.note: Score each piece on its own, before discussing it with anyone. You see only your own scores.
reading.empty: Nothing assigned to you for this issue.

flagged.empty: No pieces have been flagged for the Advisory Board.

intake.note: Check formatting only: no scoring at intake. Return work that needs fixing; send the rest to blind review, which hides the author from everyone else.

readers.note: Two blind reads per piece; a third when the first two differ by more than 20 points. No one reads their own work.
readers.noTeam: No readers hold a role for this issue yet. Assign the Reader role in Members.
readers.empty: No pieces are waiting for readers.
readers.unassignConfirm: Remove this reader? Any score they have sent for this piece is removed too.

board.note: Drag a card to another column, or use its Move menu. Intake stays with the Submissions Manager, and accepting or declining is recorded on the piece.

selection.note: Strongest first. Open a piece to record the decision.
selection.viewOnly: Strongest first. Decisions are recorded by the Editor-in-Chief.

decided.note: Author names appear once a decision is recorded.

submission.title: Submission
submission.notFound: No submission with this link, or your roles don’t cover it.
submission.intakeNote: A formatting check, not a judgment of the work.
submission.toReviewConfirm: Send this piece to blind review? It gets a blind id and readers will see it without the author’s name.
submission.withdrawConfirm: Withdraw this submission? Do this only at the author’s request.
submission.returnHint: The author receives this note and can revise the submission.

rubric.incomplete: Score all four criteria to see the total.

calls.empty: No calls for this issue yet.

calls.title: A call

partners.title: Partners

register.notesHint: Internal only. Never shown on the site.
register.missing: This partner is not in the register

agreements.moneyHint: Who pays what; how any money raised is handled, receipted and reported; charity money passed on in full.
agreements.brandingHint: How each name and logo appears; both approve materials before release.
agreements.safetyHint: Who leads on the day; safeguarding; consent for photos.

agreements.endConfirm: End this memorandum today? Commitments already made to the public are honored.

fields.purpose: Purpose: what we are doing together, and why

grants.journal_submissions: Their members may send work to Qirtas
grants.guest_editing: A guest editor for an issue
grants.volunteering: Their members may volunteer at events

affiliations.lede: People who say they belong to a partner. Check with the partner’s contact before verifying. Lists are never shared with partners.

declarations.lede: Conflict of Interest Declarations (Form F-18) from role holders. The General Secretary records receipt.

places.lede: Places with partners on Get involved: an internship, a volunteer place or a role at one of our partners. Anyone can read them; members reply.
places.new: Post a place with a partner
places.title: Title

recognition.title: Service

Qalam’s are signed by the Qalam lead and the Editor-in-Chief, the Prize’s by the Editor-in-Chief and the President.

pending.lede: Hours members logged (Form F-16). You see entries for the events you run. Nobody confirms their own.

totals.lede: Confirmed staff hours this academic year, for service letters on request.
totals.empty: No confirmed hours this year yet.

certificates.citation: Citation (the work and what it is recognized for)

hints.qalam: For a student who finished Qalam, chosen from the roster. Students have no accounts; their full name appears only on the certificate.
hints.prize: For a Mutanabbi Prize winner: the member, the category and the citation.

certificates.languageHint: One language per certificate, the one its recipient chose.

letters.lede: Service is a letter (F-05), written on request by the Director of Membership in the language the member asks for. Each carries a code anyone can check on the site.
letters.toHint: Leave empty if they still serve.
letters.languageHint: The language the member asked for.
letters.bodyHint: A line or two on their work, in the letter’s language.

forms.f30: F-30 Thank-you to a partner or sponsor

letterWriter.recipientHint: The name, then the address, one line each.
letterWriter.subject: Subject
letterWriter.greetingHint: A colon in business letters (“Dear Mr. Najm:”), a comma only in personal letters to members (“Dear Lina,”).

productions.cancelConfirm: The production will be marked canceled. This can’t be undone.

fields.isPublicHint: Only the title, summary, poster, credits people agreed to, partners and published performances are shown. Rights, auditions and the report never are.

auditionsTab.noSignups: No one has signed up yet.

fields.adoptedHint: Only once the Assembly or Council has adopted it.
fields.voteHint: One line, for example: Adopted by the Founding Meeting, 41 for, 2 against.

qirtas.lede: The newsroom is where staff write and publish directly, a section at a time. What members send is read blind on the same pages; accepted work then joins its section like any other piece.
qirtas.editionsLede: An Edition is the semester’s curated issue of the best Letters and Gallery work. Its launch is when every piece tagged to it goes out.
qirtas.launchHint: Every piece in this Edition without its own time publishes at the launch. Leave it empty until the time is known.

qirtas.publishedChanges: This piece is published: a change goes live. Record anything readers relied on as a correction.

f37.title: Qalam mentor agreement
f37.purpose: Every Qalam mentor, after training. Countersigned by the Qalam lead.
f37.preamble: I have completed Qalam training and read the Qalam Program Handbook and the safeguarding policy in the Policy Manual. I agree that I will never be alone with a student: two screened adults are in the room at all times, including breaks; that I will never meet a student one-to-one, in person or online; that I will contact students and families only through the school’s teacher, and will never ask for, give or use a student’s phone number, email or social media; that I will not message, call, friend or follow any student, in any app, before, during or after Qalam, and if a student contacts me I will not reply and will tell the Qalam lead; that I will give no lifts, make no visits, and give no gifts or favors to one student; that I will have no physical contact beyond a handshake the student offers; that I will make no remarks about appearance, keep off party politics, religion, sect and ethnicity, and keep no secrets with a student; that I will never photograph a student on my own phone, and will follow each student’s consent form; that I will collect work and give feedback only through the teacher or in the room, in sight of other adults; that if a student tells me something worrying, or I am worried about an adult, I will tell the Qalam lead the same day, or Student Life directly; and that I will follow the Code of Conduct at every moment. I understand that if I break any of these rules I will be stood down from Qalam at once while the matter is looked at.

about.title: About the Society
about.lede: To cultivate a culture of literature and creative expression across AUIB.
about.preamble: We, students of the American University of Iraq – Baghdad, gathered as the Society of Arts and Letters, in a city that once kept the House of Wisdom and still keeps al-Mutanabbi Street, adopt this Constitution so that our Society is open to every student, governed in the open, careful with people and money, and built to outlast those who founded it.
about.mottoNote: From al-Mutanabbi’s most quoted line: the horses, the night and the desert know me; so do the sword, the lance, the paper and the pen. We keep only the last two.

connecting.title: Connecting students
connecting.body: From every college, into one room and onto one page.

fostering.title: Fostering creativity

building.title: Building a community

open.title: Open and free
open.body: Any enrolled AUIB student can join. No fee, no audition, no portfolio. Members who take part in two activities a semester vote.

power.title: Members hold the power
power.body: The members elect the officers by secret ballot, change this Constitution and can remove anyone who abuses a role.

council.title: A Council runs the work
council.body: Three elected officers and three directors meet every two weeks and set each term’s calendar of events.

elections.title: Elections every April
elections.body: Secret ballot with AUIB sign-in, run by a committee of non-candidates. Ranked choice when more than two stand. Presidents serve two terms at most.

editors.title: Editors decide the art
editors.body: Qirtas’s editors and the Company’s director make creative calls. The Council overrules a selection only on grounds of law, safety or University policy, and in writing.

money.title: No money of its own
money.body: The Society holds no budget and no money: Student Life provides what its events need. The book fair’s collection is counted by two people, handed over with a witness and a receipt, and goes to the charity in full.

process.title: Fair process
process.body: Anyone facing discipline hears the concern and can answer it. Removal of an officer needs two-thirds of members voting.

last.title: Written to last
last.body: Minutes, reports and an archive are kept for the next generation. Core principles can only be changed at two meetings, a month apart.

how.title: How it works
how.categories: Qirtas: the year’s best work published in Qirtas by a student Member. Qalam: the year’s best work by a Qalam student, first given in April 2029.
how.judging: The editors draw up a shortlist in each category. One outside judge scores each work out of 100, reading blind. Voting members vote online for one work in each category; Qalam students’ names are hidden, and the public never votes.
how.score: Each work’s vote share is scaled so the most-voted work scores 100. The final score is 70% the judge’s and 30% the members’; a tie goes to the judge’s score.
how.eligible: Work published from April 1 to March 31. Pieces published anonymously or under a pen name are eligible when the Editor-in-Chief knows the writer; a winner chooses whether to be named.
